findings.rootCause: FilterOptimizer.FilterRelocator granted itself permission from *possible* binding names: meet(Join) descended into an operand when `operand.getBindingNames().containsAll(filterVars)`, meet(LeftJoin) pushed into the left argument on the left arg's possible names, and meet(Extension) never checked whether an ExtensionElem (re)assigns a filter variable. For `?s :p ?y OPTIONAL{?s :q ?x} ?s :r ?x FILTER(?x=?y)` the filter landed on the LeftJoin, so rows whose OPTIONAL left ?x unbound errored and were dropped although `?s :r ?x` binds ?x before the filter in the original plan; the same defect pushed `FILTER(sameTerm(?x,:v))` onto a `VALUES ?x {UNDEF :w}` BSA. On LMDB the mis-placed Filter-over-LeftJoin was then amplified by the null-rejecting OPTIONAL rewrite into an inner join.
findings.change: New shared helper BindingScopeAnalysis.canPushInto(variables, target, sibling) (roadmap 4.1: possible names may only block) = target possible ⊇ vars AND for each var: assured in target OR not possible in sibling. FilterRelocator.meet(Join) uses it for both operands, meet(LeftJoin) for the left argument; meet(Extension) additionally requires that no ExtensionElem names a filter variable (ExtensionIterator overwrites unconditionally). Sound because the filter outcome depends only on its variables and each of them is either forced equal by join compatibility (assured) or cannot be changed by the sibling (absent). Strictly fewer pushes, only in the unsound cases; the positive shapes (filter onto an assuring SP, filter into a LeftJoin whose sibling cannot bind the var) are still pushed and are pinned by tests. QueryPlanRetrievalTest expectations were updated: its plan pushed `FILTER(?c != ?d)` into the right join operand where ?d is only possibly bound (from an inner OPTIONAL) while the left SP `?a rdf:type ?d` assures it — the old expected plan was exactly the unsound placement, the new plan keeps the filter above the join (outdated-expectation update, not a weakening).

findings.rootCause: QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer.canPushAssignmentThroughScopedExtension rewrote Join(BSA, Extension[scope](A)) into Extension[scope](Join(BSA, A)) after checking only that A *possibly* binds the pushed names (`extension.getArg().getBindingNames().containsAll(...)`) and that isPlainJoinAlgebra admits any non-scoped Filter whose condition is not directly a SubQueryValueOperator. After the push the group is evaluated as bound probes, so a Filter inside A observing boundness of the pushed variable (`!BOUND(?x)`, `NOT EXISTS {... ?x ...}`) sees ?x bound from the VALUES row where the original scope-isolated evaluation saw it unbound (`VALUES ?x {UNDEF}` inside GRAPH). The review's proposed whole-arg assured check is neither sufficient (Join(Filter(!BOUND(?x),SP1),SP2(?x)) assures ?x at the top but not under the Filter) nor necessary (a filter-free group with unassured ?x is pushable).
findings.change: isPlainJoinAlgebra now threads the pushed names and, for every Filter, requires BindingScopeAnalysis.filterDependsOnlyOnAssured(filter, pushedNames): VarNameCollector(condition) ∩ pushedNames ⊆ assured(filter.arg) (VarNameCollector descends into EXISTS bodies). When it holds every row reaching the filter already carries the name and join compatibility forces it to equal the VALUES value, so bound and unbound evaluation agree; otherwise the push is declined. The existing possible-name precondition is kept as a blocker. The positive shape (`VALUES ?x {..} { ?x :p ?o FILTER NOT EXISTS {..} BIND(..) }`, ?x assured by the SP) still pushes and is pinned by a test. LMDB negative shapes need `VALUES ... UNDEF` inside the group, which currently NPEs in LmdbPipelinePlanCache (review 3.9, plan-cache WP), so on LMDB only the positive shape is covered end-to-end; the negative shapes are covered on MemoryStore and at algebra level (both pipelines run the same normalizer).

findings.rootCause: SameTermFilterOptimizer decided from the filter argument alone: (a) the 'unbound variable -> EmptySet' shortcut used `filterArg.getBindingNames()`, so `FILTER EXISTS { ?s :q ?o FILTER(sameTerm(?x,:v1)) }` with an outer ?x (substituted per probe) and the LATERAL right-arg variant became Exists(EmptySet); (b) the critique's counterexample: when the outer variable is also bound inside the body it is assured by filterArg and renameVar could rename the OUTER variable away (`sameTerm(?o,?x)` -> body `?s :q ?o . ?s :r ?o` + Extension(x := ?o)), whose ExtensionIterator overwrites the substituted outer value in streaming/memoized probes -> spurious EXISTS true / wrong NOT EXISTS (mode dependent: materialized probes were correct); (c) branch regression: the VALUES guard used bsa.getAssuredBindingNames(), which on this branch drops names that are UNDEF in any row, so `VALUES ?y {UNDEF :w} ... FILTER(sameTerm(?x,?y))` renamed ?y although BSA rows cannot be renamed.
findings.change: New BindingScopeAnalysis.outerVisibleNames(node): ancestor walk that collects, at every enclosing SubQueryValueOperator boundary, the names visible to the tuple operator containing the sub-query (for a Filter: its argument's names, so body-only variables are not mistaken for correlated ones despite Filter.getBindingNames() adding the EXISTS names), plus Lateral left-arg names when the node is inside a Lateral right arg. SameTermFilterOptimizer: (a) the EmptySet shortcut treats filterArg possible ∪ outerVisible as possibly bound; (b) for two-variable sameTerm, an outer-visible variable is never renamed away: the inner one is renamed INTO the outer one, and when both are outer-visible the filter is kept (bindVar with a constant stays as is: the filter is retained and the SP keeps the substituted binding); (c) the VALUES guard uses bsa.getBindingNames() (possible names only block). Tests check results differentially against StrictEvaluationStrategy on the unoptimized algebra under default, streaming-correlated, memoized-correlated and materialized-hash EXISTS hints, plus MemoryStore and LMDB end-to-end.
